summary: Brimfield fire tower on Steerage Rock, Hampden County, MA; 68-ft steel tower 1924, hurricane loss 1938, closed 1975; structure remains as antenna mount with cab removed.

facts.design: Steel towers of 68 feet (1924 and 1939), with a 38-foot first tower in 1912 and a 10-by-10-foot cab added in 1967
facts.status_note: Tower structure stands and is used as an antenna mount; the cab is gone. A state heritage report says the fire tower has lost its viewing platform and is in serious disrepair.

access.note: Rock is partly fenced around a Massachusetts Turnpike Authority radio tower. The access road to the top is disputed between the town and the owner of the lower parcel. No public opening was found.

visit.trail_note: Steerage Rock is reached by a path from Adams Field; the top route depends on the disputed access road. Confirm with the town or the Turnpike Authority before any visit.

events.note: State heritage report: a fire tower with glass-enclosed viewing platform was erected on the mountain top. Conflicts with the 1912 register date.

resolved_conflicts.field: events: destroyed vs. decades of service
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR entry says the tower provided decades of service, while Forest Lookouts and the FFLOS account say the earlier tower was destroyed in 1938. The FFLOS account resolves this: a temporary tower and then a 1939 steel tower served until 1975.

The FFLOS register says the structure still stands with its cab gone, and the state heritage report says it has lost its viewing platform and is in serious disrepair. These describe the same loss, so the story reports both and does not call the tower a working lookout.

notes_for_editor: Built date conflict: FFLOS says 1912, the state heritage report says 1911. Not resolved; the story gives both. Elevation conflict: NHLR gives 1,202 ft (366 m) for its point; FFLOS gives 1,100 ft (335 m) for the tower site. The brief's elevation_m (366.4) follows NHLR. Coordinates differ by about 0.9 km (NHLR 42.142033, -72.224251; FFLOS 42.14972, -72.22444); not resolved. The brief's status 'standing' is kept, with a status_note explaining the loss of the cab and platform. The current owner of the tower structure is not confirmed; the report names Turnpike Authority ownership of the fenced site. The date of the reconnaissance report is not stated in the fetched text; the mass.gov path suggests 2016. No staffing roster was found; the 1915 item names no lookout. Two WebSearch summaries mentioned a Pioneer Valley profile and a Turnpike Authority fenced site, but those were not read, so they are not cited. The Massachusetts Historical Commission 1982 survey and a Brimfield town copy of the report returned 403 or duplicated text, so they were not used.
